Tl;Dr: My personal ASOIAF theory is that Qyburn attached Joffreys' head to the Mountains body.

1). The giant skull sent to Dorne really was Gregors head.

2). Joffrey has kings blood; Qyburn could have gotten access to the corpse post burial.

3). Some argue that it's Robb Starks head because of Ser Robert and the German name for strong is stark or some other nonsense. Not true. Interesting history on the Strong name here - Qyburn is not the all Cersei believes him to be. http://asoiaf.westeros.org/index.php/topic/125022-ser-robert-strong-and-qyburns-little-inside-history-joke/

4). From the show - look at Ser Strongs face and compare to Joffreys. They share startling similarities. https://i.imgur.com/pN4TYkQ.jpg

5). It appears from above photo that the neck is covered. This is to hide the stiching. It's also the reason Ser Strong cannot talk.

6). The unveiling of Ser Strongs face will drive Cersei insane and prove her ultimate downfall.

7). Finally - I'd love to hear Qyburn say - Joffenstein lives!!!

What do you think?
(Spoilers) What's under that helm Ser Robert?

That is an absolutely crazy theory. I like it.

The theory seems to add up from what I can tell. The out of place scarf is definitely hiding a wound. I can see the similarities in the eyes, but I think its important to note that Ser Gregor was poisoned like Joffrey. Its possible that the same poison was used to kill both and thus gives the same looks their face.
Different poisons. Joffrey had The Strangler. Gregor had manticore venom.

I'm still convinced that Gregor has his own head. There were quite a few dwarf heads delivered to KL. One of note was freakishly large and described in detail. The details match the skull in Dorne. (A redditor came up with this initially.) That said, king's blood may or may not have been used.

I don't know, it just seems gratuitous, like it wouldn't really affect the plot in any way at all.

A zombie Gregor is terrifying enough - sticking somebody else's head on it for no good reason seems like it would be bad writing and totally unnecessary, sort of "gilding the lily" (or the reverse of that, I guess - "pissing on the poison ivy"?).

In the books, we have the benefit of knowing about the prophetic dream with the helm full of darkness, so we understand the reference in ADWD when it talks about not being able to see any features in the helm. We don't have that benefit in the TV show, so they give him dead-dude features instead - after all, they didn't send down the skull in the show, so why bother adding something else to explain?

Also, armor that exposes the wearer's neck - one of the most vulnerable parts of the body - would be very, very terrible armor. You can't use the fact that a fully-armored dude has his neck covered as "evidence" that he's had a full head transplant.

The use of kings blood in the re-animation is what takes away the gratuitous nature of the act. It is only possible because of the Kings blood.

Also - I like the visual evidence available from the show but feel that the "blackness" inside the helm from the book is a case of unreliable narrator in some sense; the idea that the "vision" of Brans is true, however, the full/proper interpretation is wrong. The vision of blackness in the helm can easily be interpreted as the dark (or shadow?) magic Qyburn is employing - using Joffreys head/kings blood - to reanimate the giant corpse.
